definition: The wake-sleep algorithm is an unsupervised learning algorithm for deep generative models, especially Helmholtz Machines.
details: The algorithm is similar to the expectation-maximization algorithm, and optimizes the model likelihood for observed data. The name of the algorithm derives from its use of two learning phases, the “wake” phase and the “sleep” phase, which are performed alternately. It can be conceived as a model for learning in the brain, but is also being applied for machine learning.

explainer.lead: The wake-sleep algorithm is an unsupervised learning algorithm for deep generative models, especially Helmholtz Machines. It optimizes model likelihood for observed data through two alternating phases.

tiers.eli5: The model guesses hidden causes of what it sees while awake, then dreams up data from those guesses while asleep, and improves both ways.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers alternate a wake phase and a sleep phase to train deep generative models. Its similarity to expectation-maximization makes phase scheduling and stability the points to watch.
tiers.paperLevel: An unsupervised learning algorithm for deep generative models, especially Helmholtz Machines, similar to expectation-maximization, that optimizes model likelihood for observed data via alternating wake and sleep phases.

explainer.example: The model learns in a wake phase from observed data and a sleep phase, performing the two alternately.
